_comment: Entirely synthetic fixture data for the retrieval evaluation harness. Not a real person, not real family data -- written for this repository.

memories.title: Sunday breakfast
memories.description: Aai always made poha every Sunday morning. She woke everyone up around eight and insisted the whole family eat together before anyone looked at a phone.

memories.title: Family trip to Goa
memories.description: In 1998 the whole family went to Goa for a week and stayed in a small guesthouse near the beach. Aai refused to go in the water past her knees but loved sitting under the palm trees reading.

memories.title: Before exams
memories.description: Before every exam Aai would remind us to do our best and not worry too much about marks. She used to say the number on the paper would not decide who we became.

memories.title: Her favourite saying
memories.description: Whenever anyone complained about rain, Aai would laugh and say "Chalo, chalo, the crops need it more than your hair."

memories.title: Diwali mornings
memories.description: On Diwali morning Aai would wake everyone before sunrise for an oil bath, then we would light the first diya together on the doorstep before breakfast.

memories.title: Grandma's recipe, kept secret
memories.description: Aai learned the puran poli recipe from her own mother and never wrote it down. She said some things should be taught by hand, not by paper.

memories.title: The balcony garden
memories.description: In her last ten years Aai grew tomatoes and marigolds on the balcony and gave away more tomatoes to neighbours than the family ever ate.

memories.title: Dancing at Priya's wedding
memories.description: At Priya's wedding in 2015, Aai danced for almost the whole reception despite her knees and said afterwards it was worth every bit of pain.

memories.title: Monsoon walks
memories.description: Aai loved walking in the first monsoon rain every year, even after everyone told her she would catch a cold. She never once did.

memories.title: Languages she spoke
memories.description: Aai grew up speaking Marathi at home, learned Hindi from Hindi films, and picked up enough English at work to argue with call centre staff until they gave her a refund.

memories.title: Where 'Aai' came from
memories.description: The children always called her Aai, the Marathi word for mother, rather than any English name, even once they were adults with children of their own.

memories.title: About Raj
memories.description: Raj was Aai's younger child and the one most like her: he never raised his voice, but you always knew exactly where you stood with him.

memories.title: अंगाई गीत
memories.description: आई रोज रात्री झोपण्यापूर्वी एक जुने अंगाई गीत म्हणत असे. ते गाणे ऐकल्याशिवाय आम्हाला झोप येत नसे.

memories.title: आशीर्वाद
memories.description: जब भी हम घर से बाहर जाते, वह हमेशा सिर पर हाथ रखकर आशीर्वाद देती थी और कहती थी कि खुश रहो।
